Then a lot of people will be like, how do I join this organization? Right? And that's what happened. Right? So the irony about secret societies is they have a structure which is like a triangle. At the very top is leadership, which is secret; you don't know who they are or what they do. But these leaders usually come from very noble families, which we call the 13 families. Then at the bottom are public members, who think their work is just good stuff. The Freemasons, for example, don't know what the leadership does; the key is middle management.

These people are the ones who do all the work and are selected for ambition—power, in other words. When you have different secret societies together, a major problem is coordination. You have different leaders, so how do you get them to work together? And after these leaders die, how do you ensure that new leaders coordinate? The answer is esquetology, which comes from the Greek word escaton meaning "the end." Esquetology means understanding how the world ends or creating paradise on earth. Even though different groups have different esquetologies, there are convergence points allowing them to work together.

Let's start with the Jewish esquetology. The Jews believe they were expelled by God from Jerusalem due to disobedience and sin, which created the Jewish diaspora. A Messiah will return to take them back, rebuild Solomon's temple, and reconstitute Israel. This temple is where God lives, and people make sacrifices to Yahweh. 

There will be a war of Gog and Magog, led by the antichrist, where the entire world unites against Israel. When it seems that Israel's enemies are about to win, God intervenes, ushering in the Messianic age when Israel becomes dominant and lights up the world.

Then you have the Frankus Sabatine. They make important changes to this esquetology. The first change is the belief that the Messiah will come when the time is right, with most rabbis expecting this around 2040 in our calendar.
